details.description: GPT-5 nano is OpenAI's fastest and cheapest GPT-5 variant, released August 7, 2025 and built for summarization and classification workloads where speed and cost matter most. It takes text and image input and produces text output, supports reasoning tokens, and has a knowledge cutoff of May 31, 2024. OpenAI's own docs now suggest starting new speed- and cost-sensitive workloads with GPT-5.6 Luna instead, and Artificial Analysis lists GPT-5 nano (high) as deprecated, superseded by GPT-5.4 nano (xhigh).
advantages: Positioned by OpenAI as its fastest, cheapest GPT-5 variant, built for summarization and classification tasks (OpenAI API docs).
Supports reasoning tokens, function calling and structured outputs (OpenAI API docs).
Scores an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 13, which Artificial Analysis places well above the median score of 7 for comparable models.
disadvantages: OpenAI's own docs recommend starting new speed- and cost-sensitive workloads with GPT-5.6 Luna instead.
Artificial Analysis lists GPT-5 nano (high) as deprecated, pointing to GPT-5.4 nano (xhigh) as the current model.
Knowledge cutoff of May 31, 2024 (OpenAI API docs).
Output is text only; the model does not generate images, audio or video (OpenAI API docs).
use_cases: Simple, latency-sensitive chat or extraction tasks.

sources.title: GPT-5 nano (high) - Intelligence, Performance & Price Analysis | Artificial Analysis

notes: OpenAI's deprecations page schedules the gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 snapshot for shutdown Dec 11, 2026 (replacement gpt-5.6-luna), earlier than the catalog's deprecation_date fact (2027-02-09); kept the catalog's date but flagging the discrepancy. openai.com blocked direct fetches (403); the introducing-gpt-5 launch page was read via a text-extraction proxy (r.jina.ai).
